text:
carmen: quick brain dump — propose we add a "predictive soft-fallback" stage to the dedicated capacity ladder. goal: reduce forced preempts by predicting when a tenant's burst will likely resolve and avoid heavy-weight autoscale/preempt for very short spikes. want feedback on product tradeoffs and launch gating.

ishaan: interesting. prediction window? risky if we mispredict and cause tail latency for others.

carmen: thinking short: 30s prediction horizon plus a cooling window. heuristics driven by recent request interarrival and token cache hit ratios. if prediction says spike subsides, route to soft-fallback lane that accepts but shapes. if prediction fails, immediately fall through to preempt path and mark an incident.

tess: need to instrument predicted vs actual outcome. otherwise ops can't trust it. metrics: prediction.accuracy, rollback.count, extra-latency-caused.

omar: infra note: prediction model must be tiny and deterministic — something like exponential-moving-average + thresholding so it can run at router scale. no heavy ML for alpha.

grace: commercial: customers will ask if we promise fewer preempts. pilot should be opt-in per-customer and visible in contract language. also need billing clarity: are soft-fallback tokens billed same as normal?

finance-bot: for pilot recommend billing at normal rate but flag events in invoices. if we see platform cost increase we can special-case. exportable ledger recommended.

ishaan: behavior variants: 1) soft-fallback on reserved nodes with per-tenant shaping; 2) soft-fallback by routing to cheaper best-effort with a fast cache-priority; 3) allow temporary extra tokens but tag for fast revoke. Which do we prefer?

carmen: prefer (1) initially — keep traffic on reserved nodes to minimize cold-starts, just shape requests to protect latency SLOs. fallback to (2) if reserved headroom tight.

tess: shaping strategy: reduce concurrency per-tenant, increase per-request pacing, and prefer short-lived prefix caching so partial responses succeed. also set a hard max duration per-burst — default 45s.

omar: implementation sketch: add fast router check: if over quota and prediction==short, consult soft-shaping token-bucket with small capacity. tokens consumed at request start. state: in-memory for hot tenants, Redis fallback. tracing tag: predictive_softfallback.{allow|revoke}.

carmen: sample alpha config snippet for docs:
```
predictive_softfallback:
  enabled: true
  window_s: 30
  max_duration_s: 45
  shaping_qps_factor: 0.6
  billing_flag: mark_for_audit
```

ishaan: guardrails: global soft_budget_pct = 5% of regional reserved capacity, per-tenant cap = max(30s * baseline_qps, 100 requests), auto-revoke when global budget > 80% used.

grace: product acceptance criteria:
- pilot with 3 tenants, one high-QPS, two medium-QPS
- predictive accuracy > 70% (predicted settle within configured window)
- no more than 10% increase in 99th p for other tenants across pilots
- billing export with predictive flag for reconciliation

finance-bot: add required CSV columns: tenant_id, window_start, prediction_label, prediction_result, soft_fallback_consumed, cost_usd.

tess: dev checklist:
- implement tiny predictor (EMA + slope detection)
- router hook + soft-shaping token-bucket + Redis sync
- tracing + metric labels: prediction.score, prediction.decide, fallback.allow, fallback.revoke
- e2e perf tests simulating short vs sustained bursts

omar: ops checklist:
- alerts: global_soft_budget > 60% for 5m -> ops oncall
- paging: prediction.rollback_rate > 5% for 10m -> escalate
- data retention: prediction decisions 14d, soft-fallback events 30d for billing

ishaan: edge cases: if tenant upgrades quota mid-burst we should recalc predictor state and allow immediate normalization. also handle overlapping bursts from multiple tenants.

carmen: UX: Console flag per-tenant to opt-in/out, UI showing predicted vs actual settle graphs, and a toggle to inspect requests that used soft-fallback. Also SDK header X-Soft-Fallback: true when used.

grace: marketing/commercial pilot idea: offer "no-preempt trial" where we apply predictive soft-fallback for a month, but clearly advertise limits. sales to prepare pilot one-pager and T&Cs.

finance-bot: caution: pilot forecasting should include worst-case platform cost if soft-fallback increases average concurrency. model scenarios and cap pilot budget.

omar: rollback plan: feature flag per-region and global kill switch. immediate revoke should re-route to preempt path; to avoid double-billing, mark those requests and exclude from soft-fallback billing exports if revoked mid-request.

tess: test matrix highlights:
- short spike 20s -> predicted settle -> allowed on soft lane -> metrics recorded
- medium spike 2m -> predicted settle false -> revoked at 30s -> preempt path observable
- simultaneous many tenants short spikes -> global budget throttles fairly according to tiering rules

carmen: risks to add to RFC:
- prediction false negatives -> extra preempts (low risk)
- prediction false positives -> SLO impact for unrelated tenants (higher risk)
- billing confusion if we don't label events clearly

grace: mitigations:
- conservative defaults for pilot (small budget, short window)
- visible dashboard + per-tenant daily digest
- explicit pilot contract and dispute window

ops-bot: created channel #pilot-predictive-softfallback-1825004321 and scheduled reminder Fri 09:30 to review staging metrics.

ishaan: timeline proposal:
- wk0: design doc + predictor spec
- wk1: infra spike + small router integration in staging
- wk2-3: perf tests + canary on internal tenants
- wk4: external pilot to 3 tenants behind FF
- wk5-6: collect metrics and decide GA gating

omar: I'll prototype the EMA predictor tomorrow and post results.

tess: I'll draft telemetry dashboards and acceptance test scripts.

carmen: thanks team. objective: measurable reduction in forced preempts with low blast radius. will draft RFC with config and measurement plan and loop back. :rocket:
